ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=3\text{cm}$, and $BC=6\text{cm}$. Point $P$ starts moving from point $D$ towards point $A$ and stops upon reaching point $A$; simultaneously, point $Q$ starts moving from point $B$ towards point $C$ and stops upon reaching point $C$. The speeds of points $P$ and $Q$ are both $1\text{cm/s}$. Connect $PQ$, $AQ$, $CP$. Let the time during which points $P$ and $Q$ move be $t$ seconds. When $t$ equals what value, is quadrilateral $AQCP$ a rhombus?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AP=CQ$ and $AP\parallel CQ$, \\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral $AQCP$ is a parallelogram, \\
$\therefore$ when $AQ=CQ$, quadrilateral $AQCP$ becomes a rhombus, \\
i.e., when $\sqrt{3^2+t^2}=6-t$, quadrilateral $AQCP$ is a rhombus, solving this gives $t=\boxed{\frac{9}{4}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point P is on the upper side AD, and the arrow beside it indicates that P moves left along AD from D toward A; point Q is on the lower side BC, and the arrow indicates that Q moves right along BC from B toward C. In the figure, AQ, PQ, and CP are connected, and it can be seen that AP and CQ are located on the upper and lower sides of the rectangle respectively, so they are horizontal and parallel line segments. Reasoning: In the rectangle, AD=BC=6 cm, and the speeds of P and Q are both 1 cm/s. After moving for t seconds, DP=t and BQ=t. Therefore AP=AD-DP=6-t, CQ=BC-BQ=6-t, so AP=CQ and AP∥CQ. Therefore quadrilateral AQCP has one pair of opposite sides parallel and equal, and is a parallelogram. To make parallelogram AQCP become a rhombus, it is only necessary to let one pair of adjacent sides be equal, for example AQ=CQ. From right triangle ABQ, AB=3, BQ=t, so AQ=sqrt(3^2+t^2)=sqrt(9+t^2). Also CQ=6-t, therefore sqrt(9+t^2)=6-t, and 0≤t≤6. Squaring both sides gives 9+t^2=(6-t)^2=36-12t+t^2, so 12t=27, t=9/4. This value is within the range of motion time.
